title: Minimum edge distance on a reworked fastener hole
text: A reworked fastener hole must retain an edge distance of at least 2.0 times the final fastener diameter to the nearest free edge, and at least 1.5 times to an adjacent hole centre. A repair that cannot hold both limits requires a new load path, not an oversize fastener.

title: Doubler taper ratio at a load-diffusion joint
text: The thickness taper of a metallic doubler must not exceed 1 in 10 measured along the primary load direction. A steeper taper concentrates load at the doubler run-out and invalidates the fatigue substantiation of the parent structure.

title: Corner radius at a cut-out
text: Any new cut-out in pressurised skin must have a corner radius of at least 12 mm. Where the cut-out is within two frame bays of an existing door surround, the radius must be justified by a dedicated fatigue analysis.

title: Mixed-material galvanic separation
text: A titanium or carbon-fibre part in contact with an aluminium alloy substructure requires an interposed insulating layer and wet assembly with sealant. Direct contact is not permitted regardless of the protective treatment applied to either face.

title: Repair stacking limit
text: No more than two approved repairs may overlap within a single skin bay. A third repair in the same bay requires an engineering assessment of the combined static and fatigue effect, and cannot be released under a standard repair scheme.

title: Damage tolerance re-substantiation trigger
text: Any modification that changes a principal structural element, its load path, or its inspection accessibility requires the damage tolerance evaluation to be re-run and the resulting inspection threshold and interval to be re-issued.

title: Flight control system change classification
text: A change affecting flight control laws, actuation authority or the associated monitoring is classified as a major change and requires authority involvement. It cannot be embodied under a minor change classification even when the hardware is unchanged.

title: Software load certification evidence
text: A software load carried by a modification must reference the certified configuration index it belongs to. A load whose certification status is not CERTIFIED may be embodied only under a flight test permit.

title: Emergency equipment relocation
text: Relocating emergency equipment, escape path lighting or an exit marking requires re-demonstration of the evacuation provisions affected. Equivalent placement is not sufficient evidence on its own.

title: Fuel tank ignition prevention
text: Any modification introducing wiring, a bracket or a fastener penetration into or within 25 mm of a fuel tank boundary must be assessed against the ignition prevention requirements before release. Bonding resistance must be measured, not inferred.

title: Fire zone penetration
text: A new penetration of a designated fire zone boundary requires a fireproof or fire-resistant seal qualified for that zone. A modification that adds such a penetration cannot be released without the qualification evidence attached.

title: Landing gear bay clearance
text: A minimum dynamic clearance of 20 mm must be retained between any new installation in a landing gear bay and the swept envelope of the gear, doors and their linkages, at maximum tyre growth and full oleo extension.

title: Access retention
text: A modification must not remove access to an item with a scheduled maintenance task. Where access is reduced, the affected task must be re-timed and the maintenance planning document updated in the same change.

title: Line-replaceable unit removal path
text: A line-replaceable unit must remain removable without disturbing an adjacent system installation. A modification that makes removal conditional on removing another unit requires an explicit maintainability concession.

title: Inspection method preservation
text: Where an existing repeat inspection uses eddy current or ultrasonic methods, a modification covering the inspected area must preserve probe access or supply an equivalent alternative method with the same detection capability.

title: One-way interchangeability declaration
text: Where a new part can replace the old but not the reverse, the modification must declare ONE_WAY_INTERCHANGEABLE and the illustrated parts data must carry both items with explicit pre-mod and post-mod effectivity.

title: Mixed configuration in a single zone
text: Pre-modification and post-modification standards of the same item must not be mixed within one zone unless the modification explicitly permits it. Where mixing is permitted, the permitted combinations must be listed.

title: Connector keying change
text: A change to connector keying, contact arrangement or backshell must be accompanied by a change of part number. Retaining the part number across a keying change is not permitted.

title: Weight and balance reporting threshold
text: A modification whose mass change exceeds 2 kg per aircraft, or which is asymmetric about the aircraft centre line by more than 0.5 kg, must report an updated centre-of-gravity effect.

title: Cumulative cabin weight growth
text: Cabin modifications are assessed cumulatively per aircraft standard. A change taking the running total beyond the agreed cabin weight allowance requires a compensating reduction elsewhere in the same standard.

title: Manual impact declaration
text: A modification that changes a part number, an access route, a torque value or an inspection requirement must declare the affected maintenance, parts and repair manual content. An undeclared manual impact blocks release.

title: Repair scheme revalidation
text: Where a modification lands on structure covered by an existing repair scheme, that scheme must be reviewed and either revalidated, restricted or withdrawn as part of the modification.

title: Wiring diagram currency
text: A modification adding, removing or rerouting a harness must deliver the revised wiring diagram sheets in the same release. Diagrams may not lag the embodiment of the change.

title: Concurrent embodiment declaration
text: Where two modifications affect the same installation envelope, the embodiment order must be declared on both. An undeclared ordering constraint is treated as a blocking pre-analysis finding.

title: Effectivity condition on a superseding change
text: When a modification supersedes another, every service bulletin whose effectivity is expressed as pre-modification of the superseded change must be re-issued or explicitly confirmed as unaffected.

title: Supplier change traceability
text: A change of supplier for a qualified item requires the qualification evidence to be re-established and the previous supplier part number retained in the parts data as a superseded reference.

title: Configuration index alignment
text: A modification touching an avionics platform must state the target configuration index. Modifications that leave the index unstated cannot be scheduled into a production standard.

title: Pipe routing separation
text: A hydraulic or fuel line must maintain 15 mm separation from any electrical harness, or be separated by a physical barrier. Where separation cannot be held, the harness must be routed above the line, never below it.

title: Control run friction budget
text: A modification adding a bracket, seal or guide to a mechanical control run must demonstrate that the total run friction stays inside the qualified budget. Incremental additions are assessed against the cumulative figure.

title: Drain path preservation
text: A modification in a lower fuselage or lavatory zone must not obstruct an existing drain path. Where a drain path is altered, the revised path must be shown to clear the same volume in the same attitude range.

title: Hot bleed duct proximity
text: A duct carrying bleed air above 200 degrees Celsius must hold 25 mm clearance to any flammable fluid line and be shrouded wherever the clearance falls below 50 mm. A modification that reduces the gap must show the duct burst plume misses the fluid line and its fittings.

title: Condensate fall in distribution ducting
text: Air conditioning distribution ducting must fall continuously toward a drain point at not less than 1 in 50. A modification that introduces a local low point must add a drain of at least 6 mm bore discharging to an approved overboard path.

title: Heater element routing and overlap
text: A heater mat or element rerouted by a modification must retain a bend radius of at least ten times the element thickness and must not cross a structural fastener line. Overlapping two elements to close a coverage gap is not permitted in any zone.

title: Oxygen path cleanliness
text: Any part introduced into an oxygen path must be delivered oxygen-clean and sealed, with residual hydrocarbon contamination below 5 mg per square metre. A modification may not call up a lubricant, sealant or thread compound absent from the approved oxygen service list.

title: Freeze protection on relocated water lines
text: A potable or waste line routed outside a heated compartment must carry trace heating and insulation sized for the certified cold soak case. A modification that moves a line into an unheated zone must deliver that protection within the same change, not as a follow-on.

title: Shrouded fuel line in an engine fire zone
text: A fuel line inside a designated engine fire zone must be of shrouded or double-wall construction with the interspace drained overboard at the lowest point. Replacing such a line with a single-wall equivalent is not acceptable regardless of material or rating.

title: Thrust reverser stroke clearance
text: A modification inside a thrust reverser or its surrounding fairing must retain 15 mm clearance to the blocker doors and translating sleeve throughout the full deployment stroke, assessed with the maximum accumulated rigging tolerance stacked adversely.

title: Ignition channel segregation
text: A starting or ignition circuit modification must keep the two ignition channels segregated over their full run. The channels may not share a connector, a backshell, a conduit or a common bracket at any point between the exciter and the igniter plug.

title: Antenna bonding resistance
text: A new or relocated antenna must achieve a bonding resistance below 2.5 milliohms to structure, measured at four points around the base flange after installation. A conductive gasket is not accepted as the primary bonding path.

title: Co-site separation between antennas
text: A communications antenna should be installed at least 1.2 m from any navigation antenna working in an adjacent band, or the pairing must be cleared by an electromagnetic compatibility test. A co-site conflict may not be resolved by reducing transmit power.

title: Proof pressure after a pressurised line intervention
text: Any pressurised duct, line or manifold disturbed by a modification must be proof tested to 1.5 times maximum working pressure before return to service. The test record must be called up by reference in the accomplishment instructions.

title: Engine control rigging revalidation
text: A modification affecting thrust lever signalling, engine control unit wiring or the start sequence requires the engine control rigging to be re-checked and the idle and maximum stops re-verified on every affected engine position.

title: Dry motoring before first fuel-on start
text: After a modification to engine fuel metering, the start valve or ignition hardware, a dry motoring run followed by a leak check at maximum motoring pressure must be completed before the first fuel-on start of that engine.

title: Reported configuration alignment
text: A change of equipment identification, part number or software version must be reflected in the central maintenance configuration database within the same production standard. The reported configuration must match the installed configuration at delivery.

title: Named standard practices revision
text: A modification should name the revision of the standard practices manual its processes are drawn from. Where a process is not contained in that revision, the qualified process specification must be attached to the modification itself.

title: Electrical close-out testing
text: After a harness modification, continuity and insulation resistance must be measured on every affected circuit and the bonding of each new bracket verified below 10 milliohms. Sampling a subset of circuits is not accepted in place of full testing.

title: Retraction test after gear or supply work
text: A modification to landing gear structure, its actuation or the hydraulic supply feeding it must be closed by a full retraction and extension test on jacks, including one alternate extension, before the aircraft returns to service.

title: Door re-rig and seal check
text: A modification to a passenger or cargo door structure, seal or hinge must be followed by a re-rig against the door rigging datum and a pressurisation seal check. Shimming out a rigging discrepancy is not an acceptable close-out.

title: Ventilation rate on a cabin reconfiguration
text: A cabin reconfiguration that changes seat count or monument position must confirm the delivered fresh air flow per occupant stays at or above the certified minimum in every zone, evaluated at the least favourable pack configuration.

title: Air data source relocation
text: A pitot or static port moved by more than 25 mm requires the static source error correction to be re-established by flight test. The previous correction table may not be carried over on the basis of geometric similarity.

title: Flight deck transparency substitution
text: A flight deck transparency change must retain the certified bird strike capability at the design speed at sea level, and the interlayer heating must reach the qualified temperature distribution within the specified warm-up time.

title: Hosted application resource budgets
text: Hosting a new application on an integrated modular avionics platform requires the allocated processing, memory and bandwidth budgets to be re-issued, with partitioning evidence showing no change to the resources available to existing applications.

title: Flight guidance annunciation change
text: A change to flight guidance mode annunciation or its symbology requires a human factors assessment and a simulator evaluation with line crews before the change can be classified. Mode confusion findings must be closed before release.

title: Auxiliary power start envelope
text: A modification affecting auxiliary power unit start capability, its electrical supply or its bleed availability must state the effect on the in-flight start envelope. Where the aircraft holds an extended operations approval, that basis must be re-confirmed.

title: Control surface mass balance
text: A modification adding mass to a control surface, tab or its attachment must re-establish the static balance of that surface inside the qualified moment band and record the measured value. Compensating by removing mass from the opposite surface is not permitted.

title: Overheat detection loop coverage
text: Where a bleed or pack installation is protected by an overheat detection loop, a modification that displaces, shortens or reroutes the loop must re-demonstrate detection within 5 seconds of a leak at the worst-case position along the duct run.

title: Oxygen container drop envelope
text: A modification to a ceiling panel, stowage or lighting rail above a seat row must preserve the unobstructed drop envelope of the oxygen mask container. The affected rows must be verified by a physical drop test, not by clearance analysis.

title: Waste drain mast integrity
text: A modification affecting a waste drain mast or its heater must preserve the anti-ice function and the leak-free interface at the fuselage penetration. A drain path that can ice over within the certified envelope is not acceptable under any dispatch condition.

title: Reverser deployment inhibits
text: Any change to thrust reverser locking, position sensing or its command path must preserve two independent inhibits against inadvertent in-flight deployment. Loss of independence between the inhibits blocks release of the modification.

title: Oil joint retention in an engine zone
text: An oil line, fitting or scavenge component introduced in an engine zone must be positively retained by lockwire or an equivalent qualified means, and must be shown not to spray onto a surface hotter than the oil auto-ignition temperature after a single joint failure.

title: Domain segregation for information systems
text: An information system exchanging data with the aircraft control domain must do so through an approved one-way gateway. A modification may not create a bidirectional path between an open network and an avionics network under any traffic condition.

title: Auxiliary power compartment firewall
text: The auxiliary power unit compartment firewall must retain its 15-minute fire resistance across every penetration. A modification adding a bracket, cable or duct through the firewall must use a qualified fitting and be sealed on the cold side.

title: Auxiliary power unit removal path
text: The auxiliary power unit must remain removable as a single unit through the existing access opening. Equipment added inside the compartment must be shown clear of the removal path with at least 25 mm margin at every point of the extraction.

title: Oil servicing access
text: A modification in an engine or auxiliary power compartment must preserve line access to the oil quantity indication and the replenishment point without opening a second access panel or calling up a higher access platform than the current task specifies.

title: Fault message mapping
text: A modification that replaces a monitored unit must map every existing central maintenance fault message onto the new unit or withdraw the message explicitly. Orphan fault messages are treated as a blocking pre-analysis finding.

title: Cabin lighting unit replacement
text: A cabin lighting unit should remain replaceable from inside the cabin without removing a ceiling or sidewall panel. Where panel removal becomes necessary, the elapsed task time must be re-stated in the maintenance planning data.

title: Cabin window inspection access
text: A cabin window reveal or shade modification should leave the pane and its seal inspectable without special tooling. A bonded reveal is acceptable only where a compensating inspection is added to the maintenance programme in the same change.

title: Attachment fitting inspection access
text: A modification on a stabilizer or a control surface must preserve access to the attachment fitting inspection points named in the airworthiness limitations. Access that becomes conditional on surface removal must be re-timed in the maintenance programme.

title: Powerplant data impact
text: A modification touching engine-mounted equipment must declare its impact on the engine and pylon maintenance data, listing the affected task numbers, torque values and build standard tables. An undeclared powerplant data impact blocks release.

title: Placard and marking revision
text: A modification that changes the content, position or language of a placard, marking or safety instruction must deliver the revised placard drawing and the updated cabin marking list within the same release.

title: Dispatch condition declaration
text: A modification affecting a system carrying a minimum equipment list entry must state whether the dispatch condition, the associated operational procedure or the rectification interval changes. An unstated dispatch impact blocks release.

title: Datalink configuration table delivery
text: A modification changing a communications or datalink configuration item should deliver the revised configuration table and the associated flight-deck message list in the same release, identified by the configuration item revision.

title: Flight-deck effect documentation
text: A modification that changes a flight-deck indication, alert or its associated procedure must deliver the revised flight crew content and alert list in the same release, stating the alert identifier and its inhibit conditions.

title: Software part number on a behavioural change
text: A software load whose behaviour changes in any observable way must carry a new software part number. Re-issuing a load under the same part number is not permitted even where the change is limited to configuration data.

title: Flow characteristic on a replacement valve
text: A replacement valve, duct or heat exchanger must match the flow characteristic of the item it supersedes across the whole regulated range. Where the characteristic differs, the modification must declare the resulting mixed-fleet restriction per aircraft.

title: Engine build standard mixing
text: Engine-mounted parts belonging to different build standards must not be mixed on one engine unless the modification lists the permitted combinations. That list must be reproduced in the illustrated parts data for every affected figure.

title: Gear position standard mixing
text: A landing gear component or its hydraulic actuator introduced at a new standard must be declared interchangeable per gear position. Fitting different standards to the left and right positions is prohibited unless listed as a permitted combination.

title: Nacelle mass asymmetry
text: Mass added to a nacelle, pylon fairing or thrust reverser half must be declared per engine position, and a port-to-starboard difference above 1.5 kg must be compensated. Any single addition above 1 kg requires a powerplant vibration survey before release.

title: Installed mass of a cabin systems fit
text: A cabin systems installation should report installed mass including harnesses, brackets and cooling provisions, not the unit mass alone. Harness mass is estimated at 45 g per metre per conductor pair unless the run is weighed.

title: Water tank capacity change reporting
text: A change to potable water tank capacity or to the number of tanks installed must be reported both as a dry mass and as a full-tank mass, with the effect on the loading limits stated at the extreme fill states.
